These intelligent and powerful omnivores become more aggressive the larger they get; the largest will kill and eat anything they can catch.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.64.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.64.

Amazons are female warriors renowned for their archers, their elite unicorn-mounted cavalry, and their war galleys rowed by male slaves.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.64.

Winged, beatific humanoids, angels are holy protectors of the weak and innocent. They are immune to normal weapons and mind-affecting spells, and usually dual-class as cleric-fighters.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.64.

Giant ants are among the hardiest and most adaptable of vermin.

Most treasure is found in the nest, but individuals may be in the process of transporting items there.

Bandits are fighters. They usually have prisoners for ransom, either with them or at the camp, 1 for every 10 bandits. Equipment within a typical band varies: 40% melee weapon, leather, shield (AC6)

Officers are equivalent to medium horse troops, but with AC5 barding for their mounts.

Bands of 200 to 300 outlaws may have a cleric and a magic-user among their number (roll 1 on 1d4 for each). Clerics will be 8th level.

A basilisk is a reptilian monster that petrifies living creatures with a mere gaze. A basilisk relies on its gaze attack. Its bite, unlike that of a cockatrice, has no petrifying effect.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.65.

Bats are nocturnal flying mammals. Giant bats always attack interlopers.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.65.

Bats are nocturnal flying mammals. Giant bats always attack interlopers.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.65.

Most bears are omnivores, and are not dangerous unless threatened or surprised. If a bear hits with both claws, it will hold on and bite, while automatically causing hug damage equivalent to 2 claw strikes in subsequent rounds.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.65.

There are numerous varieties of oversized beetles; a few are listed below but there are many possibilities. Normal giant fire beetles have three glands, one above each eye and another at the tip of their abdomen, that produce a green glow which persists for 1d6 days after removal from the beetle, illuminating a 10’ radius. Huge giant stag beetles can charge an opponent with their horns for 1d10 points of damage.

Berserkers are fighters who succumb to a crazed bloodlust in battle, often unable to tell friend from foe in their frenzy. They attack at +2 to hit vs. humanoids.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.66.

Black puddings are amorphous creatures that move with equal ease across floors, walls and ceilings and can squeeze through the smallest crevice. Their digestive acid dissolves organic material and metal quickly, but does not affect stone. Any melee hit deals acid damage, dissolving the target’s armour in 1 turn. pudding. Fire deals normal damage.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.66.

Blink dogs are intelligent canines with limited teleportation ability. They hunt in packs, teleporting in a seemingly random fashion until they surround their prey, allowing them to blink in and attack from a distance of 1’ to 4’.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.66.

Bugbears are hirsute, huge and ungainly-looking relatives of goblins, but they are disturbingly stealthy and prefer to ambush opponents whenever possible, surprising parties on a roll of 1-3 on 1d6. Their well-planned and coordinated attacks make them formidable even beyond their size.

Bugbear leaders have 6HD and strike for 1d10 damage. They are always accompanied by a retinue of 2d4 bodyguards with 4HD each.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.66.

Camels are ill-tempered beasts able to travel for up to two weeks without water, and are thus often used as beasts of burdens in desert areas.

They can carry up to 300 pounds with no penalties, 600 pounds at a move of 30, and 900 pounds at a move of 15.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.66.

Carnosaurs come in many shapes and colours, and take full advantage of their power and speed. These swift bipedal carnivores stalk prey, staying hidden in cover until they can get into charge range and rush to the attack.

If a huge carnosaur rolls 4 higher on 1d20 than it needs to hit with its bite attack, it can swallow its unfortunate victim whole.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.66.

An adult cave creeper is about 8 feet long from the tips of its tentacles to the end of its body. When potential prey ventures near, it lashes out with these tentacles, which ooze a paralysing poison.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.67.

A centaur is as big as a heavy horse, but much taller and slightly heavier. A centaur employing a lance deals double damage when charging, just as a rider on a mount does.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.67.

These centipedes tend to attack anything that resembles food, being extremely aggressive and not intelligent enough to know when they are outmatched. Their poison is relatively weak, though deadly, so victims get a bonus to their saving throw for smaller types (+4 for normal, and +2 for large).

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.67.

A chimera has a lion-like body from which sprout three mismatched heads. The dragon head is red, and there is a 50% chance that a chimera will breathe fire in lieu of its other attacks, causing 3d8 damage to any creatures within a cone 50’ long and 20’ wide at its end (3 times per day).

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.67.

A cockatrice is a monstrous mixture of serpent and cockerel. Creatures bitten by a cockatrice must make a saving throw vs. poison or turn to stone in 1d4 rounds. Cockatrices are immune to the petrifying poison of other cockatrices, but other types of petrification attacks affect them normally.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.67.

Giant crabs are found on land and under water, and often bury themselves in sand to surprise their prey. On a successful claw attack they will hold on, dealing damage automatically every round thereafter.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.67.

Giant crabs are found on land and under water, and often bury themselves in sand to surprise their prey. On a successful claw attack they will hold on, dealing damage automatically every round thereafter.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.67.

These frog-like humanoids live in the damp places of the Underworld or the Wilderness. They can jump up to 40’.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.68.

These fish-like humanoids live at all depths of the ocean. Deep ones are alien beings with an alien mind-set, who only see other creatures in the context of how they may be used to further their own ends – whatever those may be.

They continue to grow throughout their lives, and there is theoretically no limit to the size and power of the most ancient individuals (greater than 10HD are rumoured).

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.68.

Demons are a group of creatures native to chaotic evil-aligned planes. They are ferocious, and will attack any creature just for the sheer fun of it, even monsters or other demons.

The table below is only an example of the peculiarities that distinguish them; the referee should invent more to avoid repetition.

1d20 Characteristic
1 Charm person 3 times per day
2 Darkness at will
3 Detect invisible at will
4 Dispel magic 3 times per day
5 Inflict fear once per person per day
6 Levitate 3 times per day
7 Polymorph self once per day
8 Pyrotechnics at will
9 Summon demon once per day
10 Telekinesis at will
11 Teleport 3 times per day
12 50% immune to spells
13 Fly, swim, or burrow at normal movement rate
14 Horn attack, double damage when charging
15 On fire; attackers take 1d6 fire damage
16 Two extra claw attacks
17 Roll 2 times
18 Roll 3 times
19 Roll 4 times
20 Roll 5 times

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.68.

The djinn are genies of the air. If trapped by some powerful magic-user or cleric, they bargain and offer treasure or favours in return for their lives and freedom. Djinn create visual and aural illusions at will, which live on independently unless touched or dispelled. Djinn can carry up to 600 pounds in weight with ease, or up to 1,200 pounds for 3 turns walking or 1 turn flying, after which it must rest for 1 turn.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.69.

These intelligent aquatic nomads can speak (as well as sing), and often form alliances with merfolk. They have a +2 bonus on saving throws vs. spells, and can detect magic at will.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.69.

Doppelgangers are able to take on the shapes of those they encounter. They are immune to charm and sleep spells, and they save against spells, staffs, or wands at a bonus of +6.

If one can insinuate itself into a party by slaying one of its members and taking his or her form, it will attack with surprise when least expected, preferably when none of the other party members will notice.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.69.

The known varieties of dragons are many, only four of which are presented here.

The size of a dragon relative to its age is an indicator of its gender and hit dice:

Dragon Gender and Hit Dice

However, if the hoard is randomly determined it should be reduced by 10% per age category below adult, and increased by 10% per category above. For example, a very old dragon would have a hoard 20% greater than that of an adult.

1d8 Size Gender White Black Brass Red
1-2 Small F 5 HD 6 HD 6 HD 9 HD
3-6 Average M/F 6 HD 7 HD 7 HD 10 HD
7-8 Large M 7 HD 8 HD 8 HD 11 HD

1d8 Category Age hp/HD Dmg/HD XP
1 Very Young 1-5 1 1 point 500
2 Young 6-15 2 2 points 725
3 Juvenile 16-15 3 3 points 1,000
4 Young Adult 26-50 4 4 points 1,250
5 Adult 51-100 5 5 points 1,750
6 Old 101-105 6 6 points 2,000
7 Very Old 151-200 7 7 points 2,400
8 Ancient 201+ 8 8 points 2,700

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.70.

Adult dragon turtles can measure 30’ from snout to tail. They are fierce fighters and generally attack any creature that threatens their territory or looks like a potential meal. Their breath weapon is a cone of superheated steam 90’ long and 30’ wide at its end, usable 3 times a day just like a true dragon.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.70.

Dwarves average 4’ in height but weigh as much as humans due to their robust build. They are denizens of the Underworld, expert in all forms of mining, masonry, and metal craft, and will instinctively notice things like slanting passages, new construction, traps, shifting walls, and the like on a roll of 1-2 on 1d6.

They gain a +2 bonus to all saves.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.71.

The efreet are genies of fire. However, they cannot become invisible or assume gaseous form.

Changing into or out of this form takes 1 turn. The column is 15’ in diameter, and up to 30’ tall. Creatures of 1HD or less touched by the inferno will simply be roasted and killed. More powerful victims will take 2d6 points of damage from the fire, and buffeting by flaming debris caught in the maelstrom.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.71.

Elementals are incarnations of the four elements that comprise all existence. A considerable amount of the element must be present to summon an elemental, such as a forge fire or a pond. A character can only summon one elemental of its type every day, no matter what size. The elemental must be actively controlled by its summoner or it will turn on the inattentive unfortunate, and attack.

High elves, wood elves, and dark elves are slightly smaller than humans, delicate and willowy with noticeably pointed ears.

They prefer to fire from cover and retreat before they are found, repeating this manoeuvre until all of their enemies are dead. They instinctively notice secret doors on a roll of 1-2 on 1d6, without needing to search. They are immune to ghoulish paralysis, but not other types such as spells.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.71.

These nomadic cat people are independent-minded, and stay aloof from the affairs of other beings.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.72.

Giant fish come in many varieties and are found in any kind of aquatic habitat, but all are fast, stealthy underwater predators.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.72.

Gargoyles often appear to be winged stone statues. They can perch indefinitely without moving and use this disguise to surprise their prey.

Gargoyles are not very intelligent, and they do not speak, but they often exhibit a great deal of cunning in their aggression.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.72.

The nearly transparent gelatinous cube travels slowly along Underworld corridors and cave floors, absorbing carrion, creatures, and trash. A typical gelatinous cube is 10’ on a side.

They are invulnerable to lightning, cold, and most spells. A gelatinous cube attacks by engulfing its prey. A target touched by a cube must save throw vs. poison or be paralysed.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.72.

Ghouls are foul creatures that feed on the dead. They attack with surprise when possible. Victims must make a saving throw vs. poison or be paralysed.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.72.

Hill giants are primitive creatures that dwell in the hills and highlands at the edges of the Realm. Stone and fire giants live deep inside mountains. Cloud giants live in castles on mountain peaks or floating in the clouds.

Adult giants are accomplished rock throwers and can hurl rocks like living catapults, causing damage to everything within a certain radius of the impact.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.72.

Adult giants are accomplished rock throwers and can hurl rocks like living catapults, causing damage to everything within a certain radius of the impact.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.72.

Gnolls are bestial, vicious, and stupid, a combination which makes them prone to random violence and unwilling to abandon a fight. Gnoll leaders and their 1d4 guards have 6d8 HD each and strike for 2d6 damage.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.73.

Gnomes stand 3’ tall and make their underground homes in hills. Like dwarves, they receive a +2 bonus to saving throws and spot slanting passages, new construction, traps, shifting walls, and the like on a roll of 1-2 on 1d6 without effort.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.73.

Golems are magically created automatons of great power. They are emotionless in combat and cannot be provoked, though if attacked they will fight back.

Golems of any kind are unaffected by normal weapons and most spells.

Flesh Golem: Created from the flesh, skin, and bones of corpses, when a flesh golem enters combat there is a cumulative 1% chance each round that it goes berserk.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.73.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.73.

Goblins stand 3’ tall and are prone to being enslaved by more powerful beings when they venture beyond the borders of their kingdoms.

Goblins’ red eyes are sensitive to light, inflicting a penalty of –1 to attack in full daylight. Bigger, stronger goblin kings and their 5d6 warriors have 3d8 HD each, do 1d8 damage, and are not affected by sunlight.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.74.

These ancient, utterly alien beings are rumoured to be the creators of the deepest levels of the Underworld in desert regions in aeons past. They are telepathic, and are able to project their psyche backwards or forwards in time to switch consciousness with other beings, who must save vs. spells or be sent into the body of the attacking member of the great race.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.74.

system.damageText: T turn flesh to green slime
system.description:
This immobile Underworld peril devours flesh and organic materials on contact, and is even capable of dissolving metal.

It eats into flesh, dissolving it into more green slime within 1 turn of contact. The slime must be frozen, burned, or cut away, dealing damage to the victim as well. The high-level clerical spell remove disease destroys a patch of green slime.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.74.

Grey ooze secretes a digestive acid that quickly dissolves organic material, dealing acid damage every round. Armour dissolves and becomes useless in one round. Fire or cold have no effect on grey ooze.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.74.

Griffons are powerful, majestic creatures with the characteristics of both lions and eagles. From raptor beak to tufted lion tail, an adult griffon can measure as much as 8’. A pair of strong, golden wings spanning 25’ or more emerge from the creature’s broad back. They prefer to pounce on their prey, particularly their favourite dish of horsemeat, either diving to the attack or leaping from above.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.75.

Half-elves are often mistaken for elves. They instinctively notice secret doors on a roll of 1-2 on 1d6 without needing to search.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.75.

Halflings are able to vanish instantly into the undergrowth if they wish. They are superbly accurate with missiles, attacking at +1 to hit with all types of ranged weapons. Halflings are deceptively resilient, and get a +2 bonus on all saving throws.

Because of their small size, halflings treat light weapons as normal and normal weapons as heavy.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.75.

Half orcs display a varying mixture of their parents’ characteristics; some look almost human, some indistinguishable from orcs; most are somewhere in-between.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.75.

Harpies have the talons and wings of a giant eagle and the body, arms, and heads of human women. In battle, she prefers to use flyby attacks and strike with a weapon.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.75.

A typical hell hound stands 5’ high at the shoulder and weighs 120 pounds. These creatures are not at home on the material plane, and must be summoned for a particular purpose or find some other means of entry to the world of men.

They are consummate hunters, able to relentlessly track even invisible prey. The breath weapon can only strike a single opponent.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.75.

Hippogriffs are aggressive flying creatures that combine features of horses and giant eagles.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.76.

Hobgoblins are larger cousins of goblins. Under the leadership of a skilled strategist or tactician, their discipline and bravery can prove a deciding factor in the theatre of war. Hobgoblin kings and their personal retinue of 1d8 guards have 5 HD and attack for 1d10 damage.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.76.

Most hounds range from farmyard animals to large guard and war beasts. Huge hounds are intelligent, legendary creatures, perhaps serving giants in their castles or warding ancient treasures.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.76.

A horse will not normally enter the Underworld unless especially trained for it.

War horses are normally of the heavy type, able to bear the weight of a knight as well as their own armour known as barding, which provides AC5 at the cost of halving the horse’s speed.

Normal humans do not have character classes or other special abilities – they are the workers, farmers, labourers, clerks, and other ordinary folk who make the Realm function.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.76.

Hydras are serpentine monsters with multiple heads on long, snake-like necks. They can attack with each of their heads during the same round. A hydra can be killed either by destroying all of its heads or by slaying it normally. To destroy a head, an opponent must make a successful attack causing at least 6 points of damage. Losing a head means only that the hydra can no longer attack with it.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.76.

An invisible stalker is summoned by the magic-user spell of the same name. It is always invisible, even when attacking.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.76.

Kobolds are short, dwarfish humanoids with cowardly and sadistic tendencies. They live in underground lairs or deep, dark forests where stronger beings do not contest with them for land. Being small, weak, and friendless, they rely on trickery, traps, and attacks with overwhelming numbers.

Kobolds are strangely resistant to magic, and save at +3 against all magical attacks.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.77.

Kraken are giant, semi-intelligent squid-like creatures known to drag wholes ships to their doom. They can wrap their two long tentacles around a vessel to crack its hull, while the fearsome beak ears away planks. They strike their prey with their long, barbed tentacles, then grab with their eight smaller arms to drag victims into their huge jaws on the next round.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.77.

A lammasu is a guardian of law in the form of a winged, human-headed lion. It attacks with spells or its razor-sharp claws. It almost always enters combat if it observes a good creature being threatened by evil. it casts spells as a 6th level cleric, and radiates a continuous protection from evil 10’ radius.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.77.

A lamia has the upper body of a woman, tapering to a great serpent tail from the waist down. Once per day she can use charm person, mirror image, suggestion and polymorph self to lure heroes close, using her touch to drain Wisdom. When she has sapped all but 3 points from her victim, the unfortunate is completely beguiled and ensnared.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.77.

These loathsome monsters lurk in swamps and stagnant pools, fastening themselves to unwary creatures in the water. They always attack with surprise.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.77.

A lich is an undead spell caster, usually a magic-user but sometimes a cleric, who has used magical powers to unnaturally extend existence beyond death.

Immune to poisons, cold, energy drain, and electricity, a lich is only harmed by magical weapons. Merely seeing a lich acts as an inflict fear spell on any creatures under 5HD.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.78.

Giant lizards in the wild are mildly poisonous due to their diet; bite victims save vs. poison at +4 or die in 1d6 days.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.78.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.78.

Lizard folk come in many varieties depending on their native habitat.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.79.

The Mahal are an old and evil species of winged saurian, living in underground cities of disturbingly alien architecture.

Only one being can be so controlled at a time and may save vs. gaze, but if they fail they become mere puppets in the power of the Mahal, even to the point of death.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.79.

This monster is an abomination combining the body of a giant lion with reptilian wings and a hideous parody of a human face. A manticore begins its attack while still in flight, launching volleys of 1-6 spikes at a time from its tail before closing in to engage in melee. The spikes are ranged 90 (short), 180 (medium), and 210 (long). All targets must be within 30’ of each other.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.79.

From the neck down, a medusa is indistinguishable from a shapely human woman. She will try to disguise her true nature until she can use her petrifying gaze, often wearing garments that enhance her figure, but hide her face and the asps she bears in place of hair. A medusa can be viewed with impunity in a mirror, but if she sees her own reflection she is subject to her own gaze attack.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.79.

Merfolk can breathe both air and water, but rarely travel far from the water’s edge. They favour crossbows, tridents, and darts, fighting at –1 on land.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.79.

These monstrous beings inhabit the coldest of mountain regions. They are immune to all forms of cold, and are able to teleport at will. They do not speak, but manufacture devices that can imitate most forms of speech, albeit in a strange, buzzing tone.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.79.

A minotaur stands more than 7’ tall from its cloven hooves to the tips of its horns.

Belying their bovine appearance, they are carnivorous with a fondness for humanoid flesh.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.79.

Mules are sterile crossbreeds of donkeys and horses. They are not averse to working in underground spaces, at least no more so than in open spaces.

Mules can carry up to 230 pounds with no penalties, 460 pounds at a move of 20, and 690 pounds at a move of 10.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.79.

Mummies are preserved undead corpses animated through the auspices of dark gods. On sighting a mummy, the viewer must save vs. spells or be paralysed with fear until the mummy strikes a party member. Six or more compatriots will provide a +2 bonus to the save. The touch of a mummy exposes the victim to mummy rot, a virulent disease that slows natural healing to a tenth of its normal rate for ever after.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.80.

Naga are an ancient and mysterious species, thought by most to be extinct. Although they have a poisonous bite, they are far too civilised to use it in combat unless in dire danger. They themselves are immune to poison.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.80.

Nixies are lithe and comely water sprites. A group of at least 10 nixies will attempt to charm attractive humanoids. Those affected must save vs. spells or join the water sprites in their underwater lair for 1 year. Groups of nixies are usually accompanied by a school of 1d10 x 10 trained giant fish, fighting with javelins and daggers only as a last resort.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.80.

An ochre jelly is a giant amoeba; it can compress its body to fit into cracks as small as 1” wide. Weapons and electrical attacks deal no damage to an ochre jelly; instead splitting the creature into two identical jellies, each with half of the original’s current hit points.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.80.

Six of this strange cat’s eight limbs are relatively normal, while the other two resemble long, viciously-barbed tentacles. All opponents suffer a –2 penalty to hit, while the octocat gains +2 to all saving throws against attacks.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.80.

When an octopus hits a target it will attempt to establish a hold without causing any damage. In subsequent rounds it constricts, causing damage automatically with no need for additional attack rolls.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.80.

Adult ogres stand 7’ to 10’ feet tall and weigh 600 to 650 pounds. Their skin colour ranges from mustard yellow to dull brown. Ogres use great clubs and mauls for weapons, and often carry bags consisting of poorly cured furs and hides on their wanderings, filled with their repellent belongings.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.81.

An ancient, highly intelligent creature of a pre-human race, larger than a human and wholly alien in shape. Survivors are found deep underground, often in a long sleep. It flies (move 60) and fights with a weapon for 1d10 damage. It may carry a strange device that works like a magic ring or wand; the referee decides its powers.

Statistics: Journeymanne Rules, p.81. Description written for this system.

Orcs wear nauseatingly vivid, clashing colours to identify their tribal affiliation. Although different tribes are often impressed into rampaging armies, they will happily turn on one another unless kept on a tight leash by their officers.

Orcs are dazzled in bright sunlight and fight at –1 under such conditions.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.81.

A fully-grown owl bear can stand as tall as 8’ and weighs up to 1,500 pounds. Owl bears attack prey on sight, always fighting to the death. Owl bears that hit their opponent with both claws in the same round will hold on and hug automatically for 2d8 damage every round thereafter, attempting to bite at the same time.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.81.

The pegasus is a magnificent winged horse that can sometimes be persuaded to serve lawful good characters as an aerial war horse.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.81.

Pixies are reclusive air sprites. They fight their opponents with diminutive weaponry, and their aristocracy is composed of potent magic-users. They take full advantage of their invisibility and limited flying ability to harass their opponents.

A pixie is always invisible, even when it attacks. Detect invisible spells will work against them.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.82.

Massive herbivores of varied climates, proboscidians are unpredictable creatures but nevertheless are sometimes used as mounts or beasts of burden. Mammoths tend to charge at threatening creatures. Their tusks can be sold for 1d8 x 100gp each.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.82.

The body of a mature purple worm is up to 5’ in diameter and 80’ long. The creature has a poisonous stinger in its tail. If a purple worm rolls 2 higher on 1d20 than it needs to hit with its bite attack, it can swallow its unfortunate opponent whole. A swallowed creature will expire within 6 rounds and be completely dissolved and irrecoverable in 12 rounds.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.82.

Birds of prey inhabit nearly every type of terrain and climate, including some that are nocturnal. There are many different types or raptor, but they are chiefly distinguished by their size. The largest have wingspans as wide as 80’. Raptors will only attack potential prey, unless defending their nest.

Rats carry disease, and bite victims are infected on a roll of 1 on 1d20. The victim must save vs. poison or become bedridden for 1d4 weeks. At the end of this period, roll 1d6: on a 1 the victim dies, on 2-6 he recovers.

Rat packs are dense masses of creatures that can be dangerous in sufficient numbers. Giant rats are more aggressive than their smaller cousins and are likely to attack if disturbed.

A rust monster’s prehensile antennae can corrode any type of metal on contact, including even magic items.

The creature is relentless, chasing characters over long distances if they still possess intact metal objects, but usually ceasing its attacks to devour a freshly rusted meal. A metal weapon that deals damage to a rust monster corrodes immediately.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.82.

A sage can be hired for a specific task or on a long-term retainer; the quality and quantity of advice received depends on pay, and resources such as a library.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.83.

Sartyr are horned, goat-legged humans with a reputation for unbridled passions. The keen senses of a satyr make it almost impossible to surprise one in the Wilderness. Conversely, they surprise others on a roll of 1-4 on 1d6.

Usually, only one satyr in a group carries pipes. When it plays, all creatures within 60’ must make a saving throw or be affected by charm person, sleep, or fear.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.83.

Sagath are 8’ tall, ape-like beings, often encountered as foot soldiers and heavy labourers in the employ of more intelligent masters.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.83.

The largest creatures found on land, sauropods have little to fear from most predators except humanoids.

Screechers are giant, ambulatory, vaguely puffball-like creatures that are neither animal nor plant but possess some characteristics of both. A disturbed screecher lets off a penetrating screech for 1d3 rounds, increasing the chance of attracting a wandering creature encounter to 1-3 on 1d6, arriving in 2d6 rounds. Screechers are set off by any movement within 30’, or light within 60’.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.83.

These creatures are living patches of darkness. Shadows can be difficult to see in dark or gloomy areas but stand out starkly in brightly illuminated places. Their touch drains 1 point of Strength from a living foe. A creature reduced to Strength 0 becomes a shadow itself. Shadows are immune to sleep and charm spells.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.83.

These carnivorous fish are aggressive and liable to make unprovoked attacks against anything that approaches them or looks like food.

Skeletons are the undead animated bones of dead humans, mindless automatons that obey the orders of their evil masters. They are immune to poison, as well as charm person, sleep, and read thoughts spells.

Constrictor snakes hunt by stealth and flee when confronted. They hunt by grabbing prey with their bite and then strangling it with their powerful bodies.

A spectre makes full use of its incorporeal form, easily passing through solid walls, ceilings, and floors as it attacks with its deadly, life-draining touch. Living creatures hit by the incorporeal touch attack of a spectre lose 2 levels of hit dice. They are immune to charm person, sleep, and read thoughts spells, and only magic weapons will harm them.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.84.

Large giant spiders are hunters, not web-builders. Normal and huge giant spiders often wait high in their webs, but if victims do not blunder into their traps on their own, the monsters lower themselves silently on silk strands and drop onto passing prey to subdue them with their poisonous bite.

Saving throws vs spider poison are at +2.

If a stirge hits with its attack, it latches onto the opponent’s body and drains blood, dealing 1d4 points of damage per round. Unless killed or driven off it will stay attached until the victim dies.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.85.

These giant flying saurian can carry off a horse with ease. They are clumsy on the ground and far from agile in the air, but they can be trained as mounts, or as aerial beasts of burden.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.85.

Giant ticks are vile, bloated arachnids that drop onto their prey from above, although they will also actively pursue a potential meal. They drain blood for the same damage as the bite every round, unless killed or driven off by fire. They carry a virulent contagion, and victims will die within 2d4 days without a cure disease spell.

Any attack on the sensitive tongue will cause it to release its intended meal at once and keep its tongue well away from any danger thereafter.

These giant herbivorous saurians become aggressive if they feel threatened, charging foes with their three great horns and trampling them into the dirt.

The skin of a troglodyte changes colour, allowing it to blend in with its surroundings. They attack with surprise on a roll of 1-4 on 1d6. Sometimes tribes of troglodytes will use primitive weapons.

All must save vs. poison or lose 1 point of Strength per round for 1d6 rounds. The effect lasts for 10 rounds after escaping the stench.

Trolls are horrid creatures, with warty skin and ill-proportioned bodies. Fire and acid deal normal damage to a troll; all other types of damage regenerates at 3 hit points per round. They prefer tooth and claw, but they can use weapons. If a troll loses a limb or body part, the creature can reattach the severed member instantly by holding it to the stump, otherwise it simply regrows.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.85.

Unicorns normally attack only in defence, either charging to impale foes with their horns or striking with their hooves. They will only deign to carry a female virgin of lawful good alignment. Once per day a unicorn can instantly transport itself and a rider up to 360 yards (or 360’ indoors) in any direction. These creatures save vs. all types of magic at +6.

Living creatures struck by a vampire lose two experience levels. Human characters reduced to 0 level become 1d4 HD normal humans. A human drained to less than level 0 returns as a vampire spawn, enslaved until his or her master’s destruction. The target must save vs. gaze at –2 or fall under the vampire’s influence as per a charm person spell.

They are immune to sleep, read thoughts, and charm spells, as well as poison.

This animal is a bloodthirsty killer, but it can be tamed if trained while young.

Lycanthropes can transform their bodies into a powerful animal hybrid. Lycanthropes spread their curse; anyone reduced to half hit points or less by a lycanthrope will develop the same affliction within 2d12 days. Only a cure disease spell cast during that incubation period will save the character from this fate. Only silver or magic weapons will harm a lycanthrope.

It can summon 1d10 x 10 rats to its aid.

Wights haunt their burial places and sepulchres, guarding the treasures that they held in life but which now serve only to draw unwary tomb robbers to a fate of cold and never-ending undeath.

Although wights do not deal any physical damage, any living creature touched by one of these undead revenants loses 1 experience level or hit die. Normal weapons simply pass through their not-quite-solid bodies.

Wolves are pack hunters known for their persistence and cunning. A favourite tactic is to send a few individuals against the foe’s front while the rest of the pack circles and attacks from the flanks or rear.

Wraiths are incorporeal creatures born of evil and darkness. Living creatures hit by a wraith’s incorporeal touch attack lose 1 experience level or hit die, in addition to taking damage. Wraiths are only harmed by silver or magic weapons, but silver only causes half of the rolled damage. They are immune to poisons, and sleep, read thoughts, and charm spells.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.87.

Yellow mould is a deadly fungus that grows deep in dank and lightless places. If disturbed, there is a 50% chance that a cloud of poisonous spores bursts forth. All within 10’ of the mould must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. Contact with the mould does 1d6 damage to flesh and destroys wood and leather, but has no effect on metal or stone. Fire destroys yellow mould.

Full text: Journeymanne Rules, p.87.

Zombies are corpses reanimated through dark and sinister magic. Because of their utter lack of intelligence, the instructions given to a newly created zombie must be very simple. They have poor reflexes and can attack with only one fist or one bite every round. Zombies are immune to charm, sleep, and read thoughts spells.
